title: A coachman's skin is the same on his carriage and at his door
items: Joseph Daniels, Hans Johnson, Henry Windish and Charles Nelson were a shade lighter at their own door than on the box of their carriage, because the two figures were made from bodies of different skin. Each now wears the carriage driver's skin on both, with the same face.
Anyone else drawn on two bodies of different skin is treated the same way.
